packages.notes: Unloads no longer stall on an AMS 1: the AMS rewinds its spool only once OpenAMS says the filament is out of the extruder, a retry after a failed unload starts the same way, and a failure names the AMS's own error.

During an unload the AMS works with the extruder instead of against it: an AMS 1 now pulls the filament back as the extruder retracts (it never feeds it forward), and every AMS reports reverse following only once it is actually pulling back. A working AMS is never refused.

An unload whose filament does not move back (a cut that did not sever it) stops the AMS within seconds and says so, instead of pulling for a minute; an AMS's own jam during a load is reported as a jam.
An AMS 2 Pro is only asked to dry when it is idle with no filament in its hub, and a dry it does not start is reported within 10 s instead of going unnoticed.
During a dry the bridge asks the AMS to vent as a Bambu printer does, so the vents open once the chamber is at temperature; the AMS HT's vent position shows in Klipper.

During a dry the vents open once the chamber is at temperature and the moisture stops rising, and the dry ends with the vents closed until it cools; an AMS connected while the bridge runs is added at once.
When no AMS answers, status and the support report say why: a silent cable, data that can't be read, or an AMS turned away, with the reason.
The AMS measures its filament path (OAMS_CALIBRATE_PTFE_LENGTH), every load reports the path it measured, and a load that stops says why.
Stock AMS 1: loads at full speed to the toolhead (about 12 s instead of 17 s) and reads Bambu spool tags.
Stock AMS 1 support: it connects, reports its bay sensors and relays the buffer, so it loads and unloads.
